title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 406
paragraphs: So when the Arabian king had given his pledge of friendship to the men who had come to him from Cambyses, he arranged matters as follows: he took camel skins, filled them with water, and loaded them onto the backs of all the living camels he had, and driving them to the waterless region, there he awaited the army of Cambyses. This is the more credible of the accounts given, but the less credible must also be told, since it is a current story. There is a great river in Arabia called Corys, which runs out into the sea called Erythraian. From this river, it is said, the king of the Arabians, having had a conduit pipe made by stitching together raw ox-hides and other skins long enough to reach the waterless region, conveyed water through these, if you please, and had great cisterns dug in the waterless region to receive the water and preserve it. Now it is a journey of twelve days from the river to that waterless region, and the story adds that he conveyed the water by three conduit pipes to three different parts of it.
